# clickhouse_byoc_enrollment_token (Resource)

Mint an enrollment token for a restricted-access BYOC infrastructure
(`clickhouse_byoc_infrastructure` with `access_model = "restricted"`). The
connector installed in the customer cluster redeems the token once to enroll
the cluster into ClickHouse Cloud.

Right after the infrastructure is registered, ClickHouse Cloud admits the trust
of the registered cluster, which takes a few minutes. Until then the API
refuses to mint tokens; the provider retries for up to 15 minutes.

The API returns a token only once. Refreshing the resource never mints a new
token, and the token is not renewed when it expires. To mint a new one, for
example to reinstall the connector, replace the resource with
`terraform apply -replace=<resource address>`. After `terraform import`, the
token is null.

The token is stored in the Terraform state; protect the state accordingly.
Destroying the resource only removes it from the state: tokens cannot be
revoked and expire on their own.

~> **Note:** This resource is in beta. Its behavior may change in future provider versions.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A restricted-access BYOC infrastructure registers an EKS cluster, IAM roles
# and S3 buckets provisioned by your own configuration (not shown here).
resource "clickhouse_byoc_infrastructure" "restricted" {
  region_id    = "us-east-1"
  account_id   = var.aws_account_id
  access_model = "restricted"

  restricted_facts = {
    cluster_name       = module.eks.cluster_name
    availability_zones = ["us-east-1a", "us-east-1b", "us-east-1c"]
    image_mode         = "direct"
    executor_role_arn  = module.connector.executor_role_arn
    node_role_arns     = module.eks.node_role_arns
    data_bucket        = module.storage.data_bucket
    backup_bucket      = module.storage.backup_bucket
    storage_role_arn   = module.storage.role_arn
    enable_monitoring  = false
  }
}

# Minted once, after ClickHouse Cloud admits the cluster trust.
resource "clickhouse_byoc_enrollment_token" "connector" {
  byoc_id     = clickhouse_byoc_infrastructure.restricted.id
  ttl_seconds = 14400
}

# Install the connector with the token, for example with the Helm provider.
resource "helm_release" "connector" {
  name      = "clicklink"
  namespace = "clicklink"
  chart     = var.connector_chart

  set_sensitive {
    name  = "enrollment.token"
    value = clickhouse_byoc_enrollment_token.connector.token
  }
}

# Wait until the connector has enrolled and the infrastructure is ready.
resource "clickhouse_byoc_infrastructure_ready" "restricted" {
  byoc_id    = clickhouse_byoc_infrastructure.restricted.id
  depends_on = [helm_release.connector]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `byoc_id` (String) ID of the restricted-access BYOC infrastructure to mint the token for. Changing it mints a new token.

### Optional

- `ttl_seconds` (Number) Lifetime of the token in seconds, in whole minutes between 3600 (one hour) and 86400 (one day). Defaults to the API default of four hours. Changing it mints a new token.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) When the token expires (RFC3339). Terraform does not mint a new token when it expires.
- `id` (String) ID of the BYOC infrastructure the token enrolls into.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The enrollment token. The API returns it only once, so it is null after import; replace the resource (for example with 'terraform apply -replace') to mint a new one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash
# Import by BYOC infrastructure ID. The API returns a token only when minting
# it, so the imported token is null; replace the resource to mint a new one.
terraform import clickhouse_byoc_enrollment_token.connector 44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444
```
